newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bosch says six-month 1996 sales slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Bosch says six-month 1996 sales slightly higher.

text.p: Germany's Robert Bosch GmbH said on Thursday that its sales for the first six months of 1996 rose slightly to 18.2 billion marks ($12.1 billion).
The privately-held group said sales from its automotive equipment business sector during the six-month period were "on par" with 1995 sales during the period of 11 billion marks.
The company did not provide full sales figures for the group during the 1995 six-month period.

Bosch management board member Hans Hugendubel said in the text of a speech for a news conference at the IAA truck exposition that the number of products and systems sold increased considerably over year-ago levels.

Bosch said it did not include in the six-month results the hydraulic brakes business which it acquired from U.S.-based Allied Signal Inc last spring. In 1995, Allied Signal recorded sales of about 3.2 billion marks in the unit.

The Stuttgart-based group, one of Germany's 10 largest industrial groups, said it had spent almost 2.5 billion marks on research and development in 1995, with about 1.6 billion marks committed to automotive equipment.

Hugendubel said he expected full year nominal sales growth of about four percent, but added Bosch was "unsatisfactory" with its profit outlook due to heavy price competition in the automotive services industry.
